findings.reason: the section must call `_in_linked_worktree`/`repository_identity` or say why it cannot, else the census mislabels the worktree case it exists to surface.
findings.text: §2 reports "the kind of working directory it failed in: main checkout, worker worktree or temporary directory" but names no mechanism for that classification, and the owner already exists: `_in_linked_worktree` at `reckon/cli_entry.py:132` answers exactly "whether a path lives in a linked worktree rather than a main tree", beside `repository_identity` at `reckon/crew/node.py:1343`, which collapses a worktree into its main checkout — a re-derived classifier will disagree in exactly the case that matters (the worker worktree, where §1's 1,068 `CONNECTION_CLOSED` and the 467 os-error-2 launches come from)

findings.reason: unnamed, the landed assertion goes red at the worker's gate (or the worker deletes a test rather than revising it), so §11 must say it rewrites that assertion to expect the refusal.
findings.text: §11 makes `_declared_worker_mcp_servers` "refuse a value that is not a list with a message naming the key, where it silently returns no servers today", but the silent behaviour it reverses is pinned by a landed test: `test_an_absent_or_malformed_declaration_names_no_server` at `tests/test_worker_mcp_servers.py:198` asserts `declare({"worker_mcp_servers": "imas-cx"}) == []` at line 203; §11's text lists `tests/test_worker_mcp_servers.py` as a write path but never states that this existing assertion is revised, and its done-when adds only a new refusal case

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2 puts the log walk, the cause-pattern table, the grouping and the transcript count behind one windowed `reckon/mcp_census.py` function; §11 adds one key to an existing mechanism rather than a new module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 classifies each failing connection's working directory as main checkout / worker worktree / temporary without naming the mechanism that already owns that resolution.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1597, cli_options 336, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2 adds no command or option (its own text says so) and §11 adds no CLI option, MCP view or public definition, its new config-shape refusal being an instance of the existing flight-config key-shape refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §11 reverses a behaviour that a landed test pins without citing it, so it proposes a change to existing machinery it did not search for; §2 does cite the transcript owner (`transcript_index`) it reuses.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — neither section adds a pass-through layer: §2's module owns its behaviour end to end, and §11 extends the existing `_declared_worker_mcp_servers` reader rather than wrapping it.
